themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Deterioration Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints exploded to 44 this week—a 618% spike from the 6.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—signaling rapid deterioration of pavement and road surfaces across Morrisania/Crotona that demands immediate city response.
evidence: 44 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 6.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (618% increase, z-score: 12.55)
Street sweeping complaints also spiked 700% this week (3 complaints vs. 0.4 avg), indicating debris and maintenance backlog
Sidewalk condition complaints up 146% last week (8 complaints vs. 3.2 avg), suggesting systemic street infrastructure failure
reporting_angles: Map the 44 complaints this week geographically—which blocks or neighborhoods are worst affected? Interview residents about potholes, flooding, accessibility issues.
Contact NYC Department of Transportation to ask why this district saw such a dramatic spike and whether repair crews have been deployed.

themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Acceleration
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints jumped to 11 last week—a 319% spike from the 2.6 weekly average—suggesting an emerging pest crisis in the district that could indicate broader sanitation or structural issues.
evidence: 11 rodent complaints last week vs. 2.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (319% increase, z-score: 5.95)
Timing aligns with construction spike: 162 alterations and 51 new building permits filed in last 90 days may be displacing rodent populations
Unsanitary condition complaints remain elevated at 926 over 90 days, suggesting rodent-conducive environment
reporting_angles: Interview residents in buildings where rodent complaints were filed—are these in older tenements, newer construction zones, or specific blocks? Document photos/evidence.
Contact NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene about whether they've identified an infestation cluster and what remediation steps are underway.

themes_detail.label: Illegal Animals as Pets Spike
themes_detail.summary: Illegal animal complaints spiked to 4 two weeks ago—a 3100% spike from a 0.1 weekly baseline—an anomalously rare but severe signal that may indicate unregulated breeding, trafficking, or dangerous animal possession in the district.
evidence: 4 illegal animal complaints two weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (3100% increase, z-score: 11.72)
This complaint type is extremely rare in baseline data, making even small absolute numbers statistically striking
No follow-up complaints reported in most recent week, but sustained emergence warrants investigation into what types of animals and where
reporting_angles: Request 311 complaint details from two weeks ago to identify specific addresses, animal types, and complainant concerns—are these linked to one property or scattered?
Contact NYPD Animal Cruelty Enforcement and NYC Department of Health to learn what enforcement actions, if any, were taken on these cases.

themes_detail.label: Construction Activity Spike & Plumbing Complaints
themes_detail.summary: General construction and plumbing complaints surged 283% last week (11 vs. 2.9 weekly average), occurring alongside 246 DOB permit filings in 90 days including 51 new buildings—suggesting construction-related infrastructure stress and potential code violations.
evidence: 11 general construction/plumbing complaints last week vs. 2.9 weekly average (283% increase, z-score: 4.61)
246 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (162 alterations, 51 new buildings, 7 demolitions) indicate intense district-wide construction activity
1014 Brook Avenue Rezoning (ULURP) is active, suggesting major development pipeline that could be generating complaints
reporting_angles: Cross-reference the 11 construction complaints from last week with active DOB permits to identify which projects are generating the most resident complaints.
Interview community residents about construction noise, damage to existing utilities, and code compliance concerns on active job sites.

themes_detail.label: Elevator Service Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints dropped 83% this week to only 4, well below the 23.5 weekly average—a statistical anomaly that may indicate either mass outages (residents stopped reporting) or a data reporting failure affecting public housing and multi-family buildings.
evidence: 4 elevator complaints THIS WEEK vs. 23.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (83% decrease, z-score: -3.94)
This is an inverted anomaly: the dramatic *drop* suggests either a systemic reporting problem or residents no longer reporting chronic outages as new complaints
Morrisania/Crotona has significant public housing stock where elevator service is critical accessibility issue
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development to verify whether there was a 311 reporting system issue this week or whether elevator complaints are being categorized differently.
Interview public housing residents to understand whether elevators are actually working or whether residents have given up reporting failures.
